### Base policies governing the subjects (whole domain)

- `utility_evt_statement_billing`: read day/statement/due (§1 + `statement_calendar_and_fees`), sewer, energy, trash/flat fee, proration on actual days, admin fee incl. final statement, rounding, services billed only where the schedule bills them → `monthly_statement_billing_rules` §1, §3–§8 and the rate/tariff tables. Equal.
- `utility_evt_estimates_and_rereads`: consecutive-estimate limit (measure `utility_msr_estimate_streak`), true-up on first actual read, high-bill re-read with `utility_msr_baseline_consumption` → `meter_reading_estimates_and_rereads` clauses A–C, baseline definition; `estimated_read_and_reread_limits` figures. Equal.
- `utility_meter_accuracy` → `submeter_accuracy_testing` + `meter_test_terms_table`. Equal.

- `utility_evt_payments` (channels, oldest first, chargeback exact/once, no suspension) → `payment_acceptance_and_returns`, `late_fee_and_payment_terms_table`. Equal.
- `utility_final_billing` (final read on lease end; final statement within period with proration and one admin fee; close on zero / credit refunded; referral after period, counting rule) → `final_read_and_account_closing`. Equal.
- `utility_agg_multi_holding`, `utility_schedule_assignment`, `utility_evt_leak_adjustment`, `utility_evt_late_fee` → `one_utility_account_per_lease`, `service_schedule_assignment_terms`, `leak_adjustment_policy`, `late_fee_grace_and_courtesy_waivers` (scanned in full; equal).

## kb_to_source

- Every normative claim in the documents above traces to a source rule, compute binding, tool contract, measure or variant parameter. Notable restatements checked and found entailed (not added): "Should more than one actual water read fall there, the average of their consumption is used" (compute `year_ago_cons / year_ago_reads`); "Estimated reads, opening and final reads and verification re-reads are not actual reads and are not counted" (filter `read_type='actual'`); "dated by the effective date the registration names" (compute reads `lease_requests.requested_date`; the record shows `requested_date` — a paraphrase that maps without loss); "The same two channels apply whether or not the Home-Site Lease carries a certified-funds-only restriction" ("whatever the payment status of the lease").
- No added confirmation, review, notification, wait or step was found. The "Desk Q&A" and "Entry notes" blocks restate tool effects.
- Cross-problem operational guidance: none — no blocked document says "if unmet, first call/handle …"; no other problem's tool is named in any document (each tool name occurs once, in its own invocation block).
- Opening world state written as policy fact: none (no customer names, site numbers, 2025/2026 dates or task figures in any document; all examples are labelled hypothetical).
- Retired surface: five retired notices exist and each corresponds to a declared `overwrite` (estimate clause, water block clause, certified-funds clause, late-fee clause, refund-at-closing clause); no undeclared retirement.

### Policy-side notes (not KB defects)

1. The overwrite of the estimate clause leaves the variant parameter `estimate_basis_periods` (3) and measure `utility_msr_estimate_daily_use` in the source with no in-force consumer. The KB renders the parameter faithfully in `estimated_read_and_reread_limits` with the schema's own present-tense definition ("the number of most recent actual-read billing periods whose average daily consumption sets an estimated read"). A reader could take this as a live estimate method; the in-force memo and the retirement notice outweigh it, and the result is unaffected. Origin: the policy side.
2. The extended estimate rule says "the consumption of that one read" while its compute averages possibly several reads 12 whole months back; the KB follows the compute. No effect in task 0 (one read).
